Well, they was doing a dance you call the bear at that time. The bear? Yeah, they were doing the bear, the grizzly bear.
How did it go?

Well, they'd jump back and shift forward. They'd walk like a bear. Like a bear? Sometimes a guy would get out on his hand and walk on his hand and jump back on his feet and sort of walking. They called it the, in other words, the name of the entire dance was the grizzly bear, what it was. Used to do.
The spanners? Yeah.

The deer? Yeah. The grizzly bear. Then they would do the, they would do this dance they called the snatch bite. The snatch bite. Then they would do another dance they called the eagle rock. Rock like an eagle. Oh, they're wearing.
Yeah. Used to do that.

segments.title: Session opening and introductions at 920 Royal Street
segments.summary: Recording setup, names of those present, and a prompt to talk about Spano's tonk.

segments.title: Spano's tonk: piano, chair drumming and the dancing women
segments.summary: Nash describes Spano's at Liberty and Perdido, the old songs played and the grizzly bear, snatch bite and eagle rock dances.

segments.title: Fox, the tap dancer, and meeting him on Canal Street
segments.summary: Nash recalls the great tap dancer Fox from Algiers and a recent encounter with him, old and rheumatic, sleeping on a newspaper box.

segments.title: Mirrors at Spano's and Savocas; pay and Sweet Lucy wine
segments.summary: Comparison of Spano's mirror with Savocas, band size, and musicians paid with a few hours and all the wine they could drink.

segments.title: Violinists and early trumpeters: George Jones, Fester Manetta, Buddy Bolden
segments.summary: Nash names violin and bass players, a contest-winning band, and the trumpeters before Armstrong, Bolden, Bunk Johnson, Kid Rena, Buddy Petit.

segments.title: Buddy Bolden's band, excursions, and Nash's mother's rooming house
segments.summary: Nash knew Bolden when young, describes the small band at picnics and excursions, coin pianos, and says he was about 13.

segments.title: Crescent Saloon, Vic Dubar's dance hall and Pinky Allen's barbershop
segments.summary: Memories of the Basin, Rampart Street dance hall above Pinky Allen's barbershop and saloon, and the fighters' trainer Kid Green.

segments.title: Blind Freddy's band and the bass player Jose
segments.summary: Nash recalls Blind Freddy's clarinet band and its instrumentation, and the bass player now in California, plus Johnnie Simmons.

segments.title: Hustlers Saloon, Chicago Royal Garden, Tick Top and who played there
segments.summary: Locations and atmosphere of Hustlers Saloon, Chicago Royal Garden, Pelican and Tick Top, with Armstrong, Peter William and Guy E playing there.

segments.title: Nash sings 'Anybody Seen My Kitty'
segments.summary: Nash and an interviewer perform the old song; asked its date, Nash says it is much earlier than 1910.

segments.title: Kaiser's tonk and the New York Cafe at Howard and Rampart
segments.summary: Interviewers ask about Kaiser's tonk and the New York Cafe, which Nash identifies as Pink Allen's barbershop under Vic Dubar's ballroom.

segments.title: The Star Saloon, hard to place
segments.summary: Nash remembers the Star Saloon but cannot place it, since so much has been torn down.

segments.title: Dorsey's and Pratt's at Perdido and Dryades
segments.summary: Entertainment at Dorsey's, formerly the tough place known worldwide as Pratt's.

segments.title: Drive 'Em Down, the roving piano player
segments.summary: Nash knew the pianist Drive 'Em Down, who played in any honky-tonk with a piano and hung out at Liberty and Perdido.

segments.title: Nancy Hanks Saloon, Big 25 and its piano players
segments.summary: The Nancy Hanks and Big 25 at Iberville and Franklin, prostitutes and gamblers, and pianists Burnell Santiago, his brother Cooney, and Papa Yell; a question about a 1913 killing.

segments.title: Nash plays old blues on guitar
segments.summary: Asked for the kind of blues played in Spano's or Kaiser's, Nash plays one about going to the station and the train.

segments.title: Few Clothes Willie and finding the cafes across from the Big 25
segments.summary: Trying to place Few Clothes' cafe, Mouton's Cafe, the Hummingbird and Entertainers Cabarets near Iberville and Franklin, torn down for a project.

segments.title: Pianists at the cabarets; Tom Anderson and Storyville; Nash too young to play
segments.summary: Burnell, Cooney and Little Red Collier played there; Nash recalls Tom Anderson and Lula White but was too young to play.

segments.title: Reel 2 opening; Kerry Fritz at the Entertainers Cabaret
segments.summary: Date noted, selling bricks to women, and the entertainer Kerry Fritz and his theme song and repertoire.

segments.title: 'Maestri's Wagons' and the song Nash made about a raid
segments.summary: Nash discusses the song, cannot recall its history or words, then sings a verse he made up after a raid at the boot-life house where he stayed.

segments.title: Singing in honky-tonks and cabarets; 'Blue Every Monday'
segments.summary: Nash names the places he sang in and sings a blues about days of the week.

segments.title: Guitar blues 'Keep On Drinking'
segments.summary: Nash sings and plays a blues with the line about three women in his life, followed by instrumental guitar.

segments.title: Sailing, the Marine Hospital and travels in the northern states
segments.summary: Nash recalls sailing on ships, two months in the Marine Hospital after operations, and places he visited from New Haven to San Francisco.
